item.title: Glen Hansard’s Family Announces Public Memorial and Funeral Details in Dublin
item.description:
[Ethereal music fades out, and the host's voice takes over]
Host: Welcome to this special episode, where we're paying tribute to the incredible Irish singer-songwriter, Glen Hansard. Following his tragic passing on July 29, his family has announced details of his public memorial and funeral.
[Soft music plays in the background]
Host: On Monday, August 3, a public wake will be held at the Baroque Chapel at IMMA, Royal Hospital Kilmainham in Dublin, from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. This will be an opportunity for fans to pay their respects to Glen, as he lies in repose.
[Pause for a moment]
Host: The following day, Tuesday, August 4, a funeral service will take place at St. Patrick's Cathedral in Dublin at 1:30 p.m. The service will be open to the public, although space inside the cathedral will be limited. For those who can't attend in person, the funeral will be broadcast live on RTE News and RIP.IE.
[Music transitions to a gentle, acoustic tune]
Host: Glen's family has also shared that music at the funeral will be provided by his friends and family, making this a truly special celebration of his life. In lieu of flowers or gifts, they've requested donations to Dublin's Simon Community or Ukrainian Action.
[Pause again]
Host: As we remember Glen, we're reminded of the outpouring of love and tributes from fellow artists, including U2's Bono, Bruce Springsteen, Billie Eilish, and Lin-Manuel Miranda. Bono wrote a heartfelt tribute, describing Glen as "an angelic presence" and "a smiling rascal."
[Music swells, and the host's voice becomes more emotional]
Host: Glen Hansard may be gone, but his music and legacy will live on. We'll continue to celebrate his life and artistry in the days and weeks to come.
[Music slowly fades out, and the host's voice becomes softer]
Host: Thank you for joining us today. If you'd like to pay your respects or donate to one of the chosen charities, we've included links in our show notes. Rest in peace, Glen Hansard.
[The episode ends with a final, gentle musical note]
